description: Office Hours: query volume, tokens generated per day, faithfulness trend, refusal rate. Reads from the grafana/otel-lgtm all-in-one container's bundled Prometheus-compatible datasource in dev (uid 'prometheus', auto-provisioned by that image), or Grafana Cloud's own Prometheus-compatible datasource in production (Phase 8 round 4) -- no separate Prometheus, no Elasticsearch, no ClickHouse; see ARCHITECTURE.md's observability section. Query volume and refusal rate come from office_hours_queries_total, a runtime OTel counter emitted by services/orchestrator/app/telemetry.py on every served /query and /query/stream response, labeled by response_type. Tokens generated per day is office_hours_generation_tokens_total (Phase 8 round 4), labeled by token_type (prompt|completion) -- REAL, provider-reported token counts (Ollama's own prompt_eval_count/eval_count, or an OpenAI-compatible endpoint's own usage block; see app/providers/llm.py::LLM.last_usage), never estimated. This replaces an earlier panel that showed generation-CALL volume as a cost proxy: both Grafana Cloud's and Langfuse's free tiers are genuinely free, so there was never a real dollar cost to build a proxy for, and real token counts are a more honest and more useful number than a call count once they are actually available. Faithfulness trend is DIFFERENT in kind from the other three: faithfulness is an eval-time metric (it needs the judge and RAGAS, which run only inside `python -m eval.run`, never at request time), so it cannot be a request-time counter. eval/telemetry.py::emit_run_metrics pushes it as a gauge, one data point per full eval run, to the SAME OTLP endpoint -- so this panel is a real trend across however many full runs have actually been recorded, not a live-updating series and not a fabricated one.

panels.description: Every /query and /query/stream response actually served, by response_type (answer, refusal_advice, clarify, no_answer, blocked_unverified). Emitted by services/orchestrator/app/telemetry.py::record_query_metric, called from app/main.py on every successful response -- real request volume, not a sampled or estimated figure.
panels.title: Query volume, by response type

panels.description: REAL token counts, not a dollar figure and not a proxy (Phase 8 round 4, replacing an earlier generation-call-count proxy panel): office_hours_generation_tokens_total, labeled by token_type (prompt|completion), is incremented by whatever the serving provider's own response actually reported (Ollama's prompt_eval_count/eval_count, or an OpenAI-compatible endpoint's usage block -- see app/providers/llm.py::LLM.last_usage), never estimated. Both Grafana Cloud's and Langfuse's free tiers are genuinely free, so there is no real dollar cost to build a proxy for here at all. Emitted by services/orchestrator/app/telemetry.py::record_generation_tokens_metric, called from app/pipeline.py on every successful generator call.
panels.title: Tokens generated per day (real counts, by prompt/completion)

panels.description: Eval-time metric, not a request-time one: faithfulness needs the hosted judge and RAGAS, which run only inside `python -m eval.run` (never CI mode -- CI mode never computes this at all, see eval/run.py's own module docstring). eval/telemetry.py::emit_run_metrics pushes it as a gauge labeled mode="full", one data point per full eval run that actually completed -- a real trend across however many runs have been recorded, not a live series and not a fabricated one. An empty graph here honestly means no full eval run has been recorded yet against this backend, not a broken panel.
panels.title: Faithfulness trend (full eval runs)

panels.description: Share of served responses that were NOT a plain answer (refusal_advice, clarify, no_answer, or blocked_unverified, over the total) -- a REPORTED runtime signal, computed from the same office_hours_queries_total counter query volume already uses. This collapses four different guardrail outcomes into one ratio the same way eval/run.py's own classify_refusal_structured does (see that function's own comment for what the collapse costs); it is not a substitute for eval/run.py's judge-scored false_refusal_rate/advice_leakage_rate, which stay the gated metrics.
panels.title: Refusal rate (non-answer / total)
